title: 第一章　壁垒的世界

zh: 对自由主义者来说，世界并不终止于国家的边界。在他眼中，国界纵有意义，也不过是附带的、次要的。他的政治思考涵盖全人类。
en: For the liberal, the world does not end at the borders of the state. In his eyes, whatever significance national boundaries have is only incidental and subordinate. His political thinking encompasses the whole of mankind.

zh: ——路德维希·冯·米塞斯，1927年
en: —Ludwig von Mises, 1927

zh: 第一次世界大战的结束给帝国世界带来了第一次打击。曾经横跨东欧大部分地区的奥匈帝国，萎缩为昔日的一缕残影。奥地利的面积只有原来的四分之一，人口只有原来的五分之一。匈牙利失去了三分之二的领土和五分之二的人口。延续六个多世纪、极盛时横跨欧洲、近东与北非的奥斯曼帝国，收缩为土耳其半岛，仅在博斯普鲁斯海峡对岸保有一块立足之地。法国和英国当局接管了包括叙利亚、伊拉克和巴勒斯坦在内的奥斯曼领土，并声称（至少在纸面上）要帮助当地实行自治。德国的非洲和南太平洋殖民地被战胜国瓜分殆尽（南非把西南非洲划归自己控制）。这些前殖民地如今改称“委任统治地”，独立被推迟到未来的某个日期。国际联盟（League of Nations，简称“国联”）虽然以“帝国的联盟”起家，却逐渐成长为让全球边缘地带提出新主张的一处空间。
即便欧洲列强远未准备放弃其海外领地，人们也仍能从东欧的地图上看到、从伍德罗·威尔逊、弗拉基米尔·伊里奇·列宁以及贾瓦哈拉尔·尼赫鲁和毛泽东这样的反殖民主义知识分子的演说中听到：民族自决（self-determination）这一新原则正在走向世界，准备伏击帝国的旧话语。
en: The end of the First World War delivered the first blow to the world of empires. The Austro-Hungarian Empire, which once sprawled across most of Eastern Europe, was reduced to a wisp of its former self. Austria was one-quarter of its former size and contained one-fifth of its former population. Hungary lost two-thirds of its territory and two-fifths of its population. The Ottoman Empire, which had endured over six centuries and at its height spanned Europe, the Near East, and North Africa, contracted to the peninsula of Turkey, with a footprint across the Bosporus. French and British authorities took over Ottoman territories, including Syria, Iraq, and Palestine, and claimed, at least on paper, to prepare them for self-government. Germany’s African and South Pacific colonies were divvied up among the victors (with South Africa co-opting Southwest Africa for itself). These former colonies were now called mandates, with independence deferred to a future date. Although the League of Nations began its life as a “league of empires,” it grew to offer a space for new claims from the global margins.

Even if the European world powers were far from ready to give up their overseas territories, one could see on the map of Eastern Europe, and hear in the speeches of Woodrow Wilson, V. I. Lenin, and anticolonial intellectuals such as Jawaharlal Nehru and Mao Zedong that a new principle of national self-determination was going global, readying an ambush against the old language of empire.

zh: 民族概念在1920年代四处流传，“世界”概念亦然。“世界经济”一词正是在“国际社会兴起”的那个十年进入英语的。

它与一大批其他含有“世界”的词组同时出现，包括“世界历史”“世界文学”“世界事务”，当然还有“世界大战”。世界经济就像家人和可以呼吸的空气一样，总是在失去的时候才被谈论得最多。在许多人看来，第一次世界大战的结束仿佛就是世界经济的终结。奥地利经济学家路德维希·冯·米塞斯在1922年写道：“就在世界大战前不久，我们眼看就要实现一个普世社会的梦想。这场战争是仅仅短暂中断了这一进程，还是将它彻底摧毁了？这一进程竟会停止、社会竟会倒退，难道竟是可能的事吗？”
他不禁要问：“那么，谁来重建这个破碎的世界？”
自由主义者发现自己处于一种奇特的境地：他们需要重建一样东西，而它此前之所以运转良好，部分正因人们对它习而不察。经此一役，人们看清进步并非单行道——世界经济也可能倒退。经济学家、各国政府和实业界人士必须携手合作，重建全球资本主义这个破碎的世界。
en: As the concept of the nation circulated in the 1920s, so did the concept of the world. The term “world economy” entered English in the decade of the “emergence of international society.”

It came with a raft of other “world” phrases, including “world history,” “world literature,” “world affairs,” and, of course, “world war.” Like family members and breathable air, the world economy was discussed most when it was gone. To many, the end of the First World War looked like the end of the world economy. The Austrian economist Ludwig von Mises wrote in 1922 that “shortly before the world war we were in sight of realizing the dream of an ecumenical society. Has the war merely interrupted this development for a brief period or has it utterly destroyed it? Is it conceivable that this development can cease, that society can go back-wards?”
He wondered: “Who then would rebuild the shattered world?”

Liberals saw themselves in the curious position of needing to reconstruct something that had worked partly because it was taken for granted. With the war it became clear that progress was not a one-way street—the world economy could go backward. Economists, states, and businesspeople would have to work together to rebuild the shattered world of global capitalism.

zh: 二十世纪新自由主义叙事中的重大断裂之一，就是第一次世界大战。学者们注意到，在这场战争的过程中，所有参战国都“朝着有组织的资本主义和战争集体主义的方向移动”。
外国人所有的财产遭到没收，指令经济取代市场供求，集中管理的配给与资源分配体制取代价格机制；各国政府和计划委员会拆毁了保守企业机密的高墙，侵入企业的私人账目与经营事务，搜集有关生产与流通的数据，制造出一些人所谓“战争社会主义”的东西，也就是德国政治家兼实业家瓦尔特·拉特瑙（Walther Rathenau）所谓的Großwirtschaft，即“大经济”。
en: One of the major ruptures in the neoliberal narrative of the twentieth century was the First World War. Scholars have observed that in the course of that war, all belligerent powers “moved in the direction of organized capitalism and war collectivism.”

Foreign-owned property was seized, command economies replaced market supply and demand, centralized regimes of rationing and resource allocation displaced the price mechanism, and national governments and planning boards demolished the walls of corporate secrecy, intruded into private accounts and affairs of business to gather data about production and distribution, and created what some called “war socialism” and what the German statesman and entrepreneur Walther Rathenau called the
or “great economy.”

zh: 在战争过程中，私有财产跨越边界的神圣性遭到侵犯，私人资本家的空间遭到亵渎。私人账目如今成了国家知识的一部分，被转化为配置全国资源的总体计划的输入项。公与私之分的崩塌，没有任何地方比社会主义革命成功的场所更为惨烈：1917年的苏维埃俄国、1918年的巴伐利亚苏维埃共和国，以及贝洛·库恩（Bela Kun）领导的匈牙利革命。但第一次世界大战后的时代，到处都在大规模曝光企业机密——企业必须变得可见，而且据说是为了它们自己的好处。
en: In the course of the war, the sacred nature of private property across borders was violated; the space of the private capitalist was desecrated. Private accounts were now part of state knowledge, rendered as inputs into a comprehensive plan for allocating the nation’s resources. Nowhere was the collapse of the division between public and private more catastrophic than in the sites of successful socialist revolutions: the Soviet Union in 1917, the Bavarian Soviet republic of 1918, and the Hungarian revolution under Bela Kun. But the era after the First World War saw everywhere a great exposure of corporate secrets—business had to be made visible, and for its own good.

zh: 从自由主义的视角看，战后有三个因素壮大了政治领域、压过了经济领域。第一，欧洲和北美男子普选权的普遍化强化了人民主权，使人们更难再靠将国内经济调整的代价转嫁给普通民众来维持金本位制。

第二，战争留下了一份遗产，即自由主义者认为人们误信政府有能力配置资源。米塞斯与哈耶克在维也纳最重要的论敌之一是奥托·内伊拉斯（Otto Neurath），此人曾为巴伐利亚共和国设计过一个取消货币的经济计划——这绝非巧合。自战争以来，由中央机构指挥的经济看起来成了一种可行的替代方案。第三，凡尔赛和约与圣日耳曼和约对战争的处置，验证了这样的观念：民族是组织人类事务最重要的范畴。在后来将成为新自由主义者的那群人看来，1918年之后的时代，其特征是试图重建他们眼中的正确平衡——政府这一公共世界与财产和契约这一私人世界之间的平衡。具体而言，这体现为一系列资本主义国际主义的规划。必须存在一种高于国家法律的、对私有财产的尊重；投资必须能够自由往返地跨越边界，不必担心障碍或征用；资本必须重新摆脱国界的束缚。
en: From the liberal perspective, three factors empowered the domain of politics against that of the economy after the war. First, popular sovereignty was strengthened by the generalization of universal male suffrage in Europe and North America, making it more difficult to maintain the gold standard through domestic adjustments borne by ordinary people.

Second, the war left a legacy of what liberals saw as misguided confidence in the power of governments to allocate resources. It is no coincidence that one of Hayek and Mises’s most important antagonists in Vienna was Otto Neurath, a man who had created a moneyless plan for the Bavarian Republic. Since the war, an economy directed by central authorities looked like a viable alternative. Third, the resolution of the war in the peace treaties of Versailles and St. Germain validated the idea that the nation was the most important category for organizing human affairs. To the group that would become the neoliberals, the era after 1918 was marked by an attempt to reestablish what they saw as the correct balance between the public world of government and the private world of property and contract. Concretely, this translated into a series of projects of capitalist internationalism. There needed to be a respect for private property that trumped national law. Investment must be able to cross borders back and forth without fear of obstacles or expropriation. Capital needed to become cosmopolitan again.

zh: 本章将聚焦1920年代维也纳的奥地利自由主义者，以及他们最初磨砺技艺、形成政治世界观的那些机构。这一时期最重要的两个国际经济机构是国际商会（International Chamber of Commerce，ICC）和国联。正是这两个机构组织了1927年世界经济会议——第一次把整个世界作为讨论对象的经济会议。会议将国际社会反对贸易障碍的立场写成正式决议，并使“关税壁垒”（tariff wall）这个比喻得到广泛使用。在美国退入相对外交孤立的年代，国联率先起草全球经济治理的蓝图；后来的新自由主义者路德维希·冯·米塞斯、戈特弗里德·哈伯勒、威廉·勒普克（Wilhelm Röpke）、莱昂内尔·罗宾斯和F. A. 哈耶克，全都直接参与了这一系列讨论。
en: In this chapter I will focus on the Austrian liberals in the Vienna of the 1920s and the institutions where they first practiced their craft and found their political worldview. The two most important international economic institutions of the period were the International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) and the League of Nations. Those two institutions organized the World Economic Conference of 1927, the first economic gathering to take the entire world as its subject. It codified an international opposition to trade obstacles and brought the metaphor of the “tariff wall” into common circulation. In an era when the United States withdrew into relative diplomatic isolation, the League of Nations took the lead in drafting blueprints for global economic governance, a series of conversations in which the later neoliberals Ludwig von Mises, Gottfried Haberler, Wilhelm Röpke, Lionel Robbins, and F. A. Hayek were all directly involved.

zh: 对这些机构来说，一个挑战是恢复自由贸易，另一个挑战则是工会这一国内障碍。就在世界经济会议召开的同一年，米塞斯在维也纳目睹了工人起义——近百人丧生，司法宫陷于火海。在自由主义者眼中，关税壁垒和工人的工资要求是市场上的两种路障。要实现自由主义的理想，就需要这样一个国家：它既能清除贸易的障碍，也能清除工资调整的障碍。这意味着要坚决对抗有组织的劳工保住工资和国家授予的权益的做法，必要时动用武装力量。1927年暴动遭血腥镇压一事让米塞斯确信：国家愿意也有能力不择手段，阻止工人制造有利于自身目标的政治条件。
en: One challenge for the institutions was to restore free trade; the other was the domestic obstacle of labor unions. In the same year as the World Economic Conference, Mises was present for the workers’ uprising in Vienna, which left close to one hundred people dead and the Palace of Justice in flames. Liberals perceived tariff walls and workers’ wage demands as two kinds of barricades in the market. Achieving the liberal ideal required a state that could eliminate obstacles to trade and obstacles to the adjustment of wages. This meant a militant and, when necessary, militarized opposition to the strategies of organized labor to protect their salaries and their state-granted entitlements. The bloody suppression of the 1927 riots assured Mises that the state was willing and able to use any means necessary to prevent workers from creating political conditions favorable to their own goals.

zh: 环城大道（Ringstrasse）上的战斗自由主义

如果说有组织的新自由主义有一个诞生地，那就是维也纳宏伟的环城大道东端的 Stubenring 8—10号。1907年，下奥地利工商会（后称维也纳工商会）在这个地址开设了新厦。这座六层巨构由路德维希·鲍曼（Ludwig Baumann）设计，新古典主义与青年风格（Jugendstil）新艺术混合并陈，转角处高踞着双元帝国的双头鹰，盾徽上刻着捆扎的束棒。走进大楼要穿过四根大理石柱，然后登上中央大楼梯；楼梯两侧立着真人大小的青铜像——赤裸上身的埃及侍童高举祭碗，身后是蓝绿镶嵌玻璃拼成的几何格栅。路德维希·米塞斯1909年27岁入职此处，在此后的二十五年里每个工作日都拾级而上。F. A. 哈耶克1921年在这里得到第一份工作，与米塞斯一起以公务员身份在一个处理圣日耳曼和约相关事务的委员会共事十八个月。

1920年代中期以后，哈耶克重回米塞斯身边，另一位门生戈特弗里德·哈伯勒也加入进来——米塞斯为这两人在同楼办公的奥地利商业周期研究所谋得了职位。米塞斯面朝环城大道的二楼办公室，也是他私人研讨班的开会场所；参加者包括弗里茨·马赫卢普（Fritz Machlup），莱昂内尔·罗宾斯、弗兰克·奈特和约翰·范西克尔也前来访问。这个研讨班后来成为一个“学界之外形成的世界主义知识群体”的组成部分。这个群体在1947年发展为新自由主义的朝圣山学社（Mont Pèlerin Society）。
en: If organized neoliberalism has a birthplace, it is Stubenring 8–10 at the eastern end of the grand boulevard of Vienna’s Ringstrasse. At that address, in 1907, the Lower Austrian Chamber of Commerce and Industry (later the Vienna Chamber of Commerce) opened its new building, a massive six-story structure designed by Ludwig Baumann in a combination of neoclassicism and Jugendstil art nouveau, with the two-headed eagle of the dual monarchy on its corner with the bound fasces on a shield. One entered the building between four marble columns, then proceeded up a central stairway flanked by life-size bronze sculptures of topless Egyptian acolytes holding votive bowls aloft and backed by a geometric matrix of blue and green stained glass. After taking a job there in 1909 at age 27, Ludwig Mises walked up those stairs every working day for twenty-five years. F. A. Hayek took his first job there in 1921, working with Mises as a civil servant for eighteen months on a commission related to the St. Germain peace treaty.

After the mid1920s, Mises was joined by Hayek again, along with another protégé, Gottfried Haberler, for whom Mises secured positions in the Austrian Business Cycle Research Institute, which operated in the same building. Mises’s office on the second floor, facing the Ringstrasse, was also the meeting place for his private seminar, which included Fritz Machlup and visits by Lionel Robbins, Frank Knight, and John Van Sickle, becoming part of the “extra-academic cosmopolitan intellectual formation” that in 1947 would become the neoliberal Mont Pèlerin Society.

zh: 把新自由主义的故事从1920年代的 Stubenring 讲起，而不是从1947年的朝圣山（Mont Pèlerin）讲起，就能戳破那种孤军奋战的知识分子的自我英雄化叙事，显露未来新自由主义者形成其信条的世界。这也表明，他们的写作始于直截了当的政策问题，而非抽象玄思。尽管米塞斯声称“没有任何职业比大学教授更令我向往”，但在许多方面，工商会始终是他最典型的活动舞台，他的政策主张也惊人的一以贯之。
他在奥地利的职业生涯始于哈布斯堡帝国（Habsburg Empire）的最后岁月，当时他极力主张减轻工业企业的税负；而到第一奥地利共和国的最后岁月结束这段生涯时，他主张的还是同一件事。米塞斯1918年出任工商会秘书，有义务在两次世界大战之间（即“战间期”）为政府提供咨询、为新法律撰写专家评估；这项职责在1930年他领导一个三人经济委员会时达到顶峰。
尽管人们铭记的是他在社会哲学以及货币与信用理论方面的研究，米塞斯成年后的大半生，其实是以直率的商业利益代言人身份谋生的——1920和1930年代在工商会，移居美国之后则在全国制造商协会（NAM）和经济教育基金会（Foundation for Economic Education）。
en: Beginning the story of neoliberalism with the Stubenring in the 1920s rather than with Mont Pèlerin in 1947 deflates the self-heroizing narrative of lonely embattled intellectuals and reveals the world in which future neoliberals formed their principles. It also shows how their writing began with straightforward policy problems rather than abstract contemplation. Though Mises claimed that “no other calling was more desirable to me as that of a university professor,” in many ways the Chamber of Commerce remained his most characteristic milieu, and his policy suggestions remained remarkably consistent.

He began his career in Austria in the last years of the Habsburg Empire, advocating strenuously for lower corporate taxes on industry, and ended it in the last years of the First Austrian Republic, arguing for the same. Taking the position of Chamber secretary in 1918, Mises was obliged to advise the government and write expert evaluations of new laws in the interwar period, a duty that peaked with leading a three-person Economic Commission in 1930.

Even if he is remembered for his work on social philosophy and theories of money and credit, Mises earned his livelihood for much of his adult life as a forthright advocate for the needs of business, including with the Chamber of Commerce in the 1920s and 1930s, and the National Association of Manufacturers (NAM) and Foundation for Economic Education after his emigration to the United States.

zh: 维也纳工商会坐落于环城大道，这个位置意味深长，有助于说明奥地利支系的新自由主义脱胎于怎样的环境。环城大道本身建于1848年革命之后，建在昔日中世纪城墙拆除后留下的空地上。在关于世纪末维也纳的经典研究中，卡尔·舒尔什克（Carl Schorske）描述了自由派主政的市政府如何把环城大道用作展示其社会秩序愿景的舞台：议会大厦和市政厅与剧院、大学比邻而建。
这里的建设呼应着乔治-欧仁·奥斯曼男爵（Baron George-Eugène Haussmann）主持下的巴黎改造。两个城市更新项目都在中世纪城市里辟出商业与交通的动脉：大街宽阔，两侧的歌剧院和博物馆是文化教养的场所，纪念碑宣示国家权力，橱窗和街边咖啡馆提供消费——一条街同时兼负多能。
宽阔的街道还会让未来的起义者更难筑起1848年革命中那种标志性的路障。两个规划都配有军械库和兵营，便于迅速调兵平定内患。
环城大道和奥斯曼的林荫大道把维也纳和巴黎变成了现代城市：商业的枢纽，足以容纳——也足以管治——不断增长的各个阶层的人口。
en: The location of the Vienna Chamber of Commerce on the Ringstrasse was heavy with symbolism and helps illustrate the milieu out of which the Austrian strain of neoliberalism emerged. The boulevards themselves were built in the wake of the revolutions of 1848 on the vacant land that had once been the medieval city walls. In his classic study of fin-de-siècle Vienna, Carl Schorske describes how the liberal city government used the Ringstrasse to showcase its vision of social order, building the parliament and city hall alongside theaters and the university.

The developments echoed those under way in Paris under the direction of Baron George-Eugène Haussmann. Both urban renewal projects created arteries of commerce and transportation in medieval cities, building wide streets that could serve simultaneously as sites of cultural enrichment in their opera houses and museums, expressions of state power in their monuments, and sites of consumption in their shop windows and sidewalk cafes.

The wide streets would also make it harder for future insurgents to build the barricades that characterized the revolutions of 1848. Both designs included arsenals and barracks for the easy deployment of troops to quell domestic threats.
The Ringstrasse and Haussmann’s boulevards turned Vienna and Paris into modern cities, hubs of commerce capable of accommodating—and policing—an expanding population of all classes.

zh: Stuben 区建在环城大道的末端，落成于1900年代的头十年，“就在自由派时代落幕之际”。

从工商会大楼望出去，对面便是七层高的战争部大楼，出自同一位建筑师之手，1913年竣工。楼顶立着一只翼展十六米的青铜哈布斯堡鹰，为了承托它，特意加建了一层楼。鹰下有一句口号：“欲求和平，必先备战。”战后，这座大楼成了奥地利军队的营房。鹰还在，但实实在在被剥去了皇冠，口号也被撤下。这组建筑群中的第三座大楼原封未动：邮政储蓄银行总部，同样体量巨大，由奥托·瓦格纳（Otto Wagner）设计，1906年落成，是青年风格与早期现代主义最著名的建筑之一——钢筋混凝土筑造，立面大胆地摒弃装饰。
en: The Stuben Quarter was built at the tail end of the Ringstrasse in the first decade of the 1900s, “as the liberal era closed.”

The view from the Chamber of Commerce was onto the massive seven-story War Ministry, designed by the same architect and completed in 1913. That building was topped by a bronze Habsburg eagle with a sixteen-meter wingspan, which required that an extra floor be built to undergird it. Beneath it was a slogan: “If you want peace, prepare for war.” After the war, the building became a barracks for the Austrian military. The eagle remained but was literally decrowned, and the slogan was removed. The third building in the ensemble remained unchanged: the headquarters of the Postal Savings Bank, an equally massive building designed by Otto Wagner, which opened in 1906 as one of the most famous buildings in the style of Jugendstil and early modernism, built with reinforced concrete with a facade boldly free of ornament.

zh: 米塞斯在 Stuben 区这个位置上注视着这十年的事态，形成了他的经济秩序观。与维也纳工商会隔街相望的战争部大楼，似乎具体体现了米塞斯日后要反对的“全能政府”（omnipotent government）。
然而，他的新自由主义从未笼统地排斥国家。
米歇尔·福柯（Michel Foucault）说奥地利新自由主义者患有“国家恐惧症”（state-phobia），这是一种误解——尤其考虑到米塞斯作为长期主张以税收资助工商界利益相关事项的经历。
米塞斯日后会成为美国自由至上主义者（libertarians）的守护神，但他不仅以政府出资的顾问为职业，也为国家在保护财产、维持治安方面的强力角色留有位置。1922年，他在一个意味深长的说法中称国家为“安全的生产者”。
对米塞斯来说，评估国家行动要看它作用于哪个领域。帝国国家本身并不让他操心。他害怕的是那种诉诸“人民”以取得合法性的干预主义政府。他心中的国家，其合法性只能来自对私有财产神圣性与竞争力量的捍卫。
en: Mises watched the events of the decade and formed his vision of economic order from the vantage point of the Stuben Quarter. The War Ministry building across the street from the Vienna Chamber of Commerce seemed to embody what Mises would later oppose as “omnipotent government.”
Yet his version of neoliberalism never rejected the state as such.

Michel Foucault’s attribution of “state-phobia” to Austrian neoliberals is a misunderstanding, especially considering Mises’s career as an advocate for the use of government taxes to fund business interests.

Mises would become a patron saint to American libertarians, but he not only worked professionally as a state-funded advisor to the government but also saw a strong role for the state in the protection of property and keeping of the peace. In a telling phrase from 1922, he called the state “a producer of security.”

For Mises, the assessment of state action depended on the field of engagement. The imperial state itself did not concern him. His fear was of interventionist government that appealed to “the people” for its legitimacy. His state could find its legitimacy only in its defense of the sanctity of private property and the forces of competition.

zh: 第3章将会看到，米塞斯动用政府军事力量去打开并巩固海外市场，毫无顾忌。而尽管他谴责自己所谓的“国家主义”（étatism）——国家对商品生产和供给的干预——他却批评国家在对付工会时出手不够狠。
维护治安往往意味着镇压工人示威，而在他看来，这类示威就是法外的犯罪暴力。这样的职能既不是、也不可能是“小国家”的职能。从这个意义上说，旧战争部大楼在1920年之后变为新奥地利军队的驻军营房，也应被看作米塞斯新自由主义模式中必要而恰当的组成部分。
en: We will see in Chapter 3 that Mises had no qualms about using government military power to open and secure overseas markets. And even as he condemned what he called “étatism”—state intervention into the production and supply of goods—he criticized the state for not acting more aggressively against labor unions.

Maintaining security often involved repressing worker demonstrations, which he saw as criminal violence outside of the law. Such undertakings were not and could not be the functions of a small state. In this sense, the transformation of the former War Ministry into a garrison for the new Austrian military after 1920 should also be seen as a necessary and appropriate component of Mises’s neoliberal model.

zh: 舒尔什克断言，二十世纪初是自由派时代的终结。就政党政治而言也许如此，但1907年同样是男子普选权实现之年——而这正是自由主义为实现人民主权提出的核心诉求之一。它的取得部分靠的正是直接行动，包括1907年的街头示威，而这一点让米塞斯深受震动。他把公众示威描述为“恐怖与恐吓”的手段。他在回忆录中写道：“社会民主党人自认拥有‘占据街头的权利’，却无人对此提出异议。”

维也纳的街道，尤其是环城大道，不只是象征性的空间。它们是表达民众诉求的论坛——诉求有时得到满足，有时遭到压制。在起义的时刻，人群本身成为“人民”的象征；而那些怀疑民主的人，往往就根据这类景象来构建其对变革的抵抗。城市不只是这套特定思想得以登场的背景板。新自由主义思想者正是针对他们眼前所见的世界才形成其观念的。在奥地利实行普选权的时代，民主问题变得愈发紧迫。可以说，所谓“自由派时代的终结”——作为一种军事化自由主义新范式（后来被称为新自由主义）的登场——恰恰是对大众民主成长的一种回应。这一新范式不以议会或大学为中心，而以 Stuben 区里安全、金融、商业三者组成的三头同盟为中枢。装备精良的国家和稳健的货币，辅以工商界——这就是正在成形的意识形态的徽记。
en: Schorske claimed that the early twentieth century was the end of the liberal era. That might be true for party politics, but 1907 was also the year of the achievement of universal male suffrage, one of liberalism’s central demands for achieving popular sovereignty. It was partly direct action, including demonstrations in 1907, that brought this about, and this shook Mises deeply. He described public demonstrations as tactics of “terror and intimidation.” “Unchallenged,” he wrote in his memoirs, “the Social Democrats assumed the ‘right to the street.’ ”

The streets of Vienna, and the Ringstrasse in particular, were more than a symbolic space. They were the forum where popular demands were voiced, sometimes to be granted and other times to be suppressed. In moments of uprising, crowds became symbols for the people as such, and those who were skeptical of democracy often based their resistance to change on the sight of such manifestations. The city was not just the backdrop for the emergence of a particular set of ideas. Neoliberal thinkers arrived at their ideas in response to the world they saw around them. The question of democracy became more pressing in the era of universal suffrage in Austria. One could argue that the “end of the liberal era”—as the advent of a new paradigm of militarized liberalism, later to be called neoliberalism—developed precisely as a response to the growth of mass democracy. This new paradigm was centered, not in the parliament or university, but in the triumvirate of security, finance, and commerce located in the Stuben Quarter. A well-armed state and sound money flanked by business were the icons of the ideology taking shape.

zh: 第一次世界大战之后，米塞斯及其圈子在民族国家与帝国之外找到了制度性的盟友。重建米塞斯所称全球经济之“破碎世界”的一个关键机构，是1920年在巴黎成立的国际商会。近来那些关于国际公民社会的历史著作，对企业家的国际协调——资本家的全球公共领域——给予的关注少得令人惊讶。关于国际商会这个最具典范性的组织，只出版过两本书：一篇德语博士论文，以及1930年代由商会自身委托撰写的一本著作；后者书名——《和平商人》（
）——便暗示了其内部立场。
国际商会日后成为奥地利新自由主义者重要的制度伙伴。
en: After the First World War, Mises and his circle found institutional allies beyond the nation and empire. A key institution in rebuilding what Mises called the “shattered world” of the global economy was the ICC, founded in Paris in 1920. The many recent histories of international civil society have given surprisingly little attention to the international coordination of businesspeople: the global public sphere of capitalists. Only two books have been written about its most paradigmatic organization, the ICC: a dissertation in German, and a book commissioned by the chamber itself in the 1930s, with a title—
—that suggests an in-house bias.
The ICC would become an important institutional partner for the Austrian neoliberals.

zh: 国际商会脱胎于十九世纪末两股潮流的合流：国际卡特尔与国际统计协会。卡特尔是同一行业的实业家组成的集团，用来定价并确保集体盈利。国际商会的直接先驱，是第一次世界大战前十来年出现的国际商业联合会；它们把原先讳莫如深的卡特尔协商公之于众，并将公共关系的成分纳入自身实践。
国际统计协会则始于国际统计学会。该学会成立于1885年，是第一个汇编全球统计数据的实体。学会由维也纳大学的两位经济学家主持，二人同时也是米塞斯的老师：弗朗茨·诺伊曼-施帕尔特（Franz Neumann-Spallart）和弗朗茨·尤拉谢克（Franz Juraschek）。尤拉谢克是F. A. 哈耶克的外祖父，与这个新自由主义圈子有骨肉之亲。
en: The ICC emerged as an amalgam of two developments in the late nineteenth century: international cartels and international statistical associations. The cartels were groups of businessmen who specialized in the same sector and would set prices and ensure collective profitability. The ICC’s direct forerunners were international business federations that appeared in the decade before the First World War. These made public the formerly secretive cartel discussions and incorporated an aspect of public relations into their practice.

The international statistical associations began with the International Statistical Institute, which was formed in 1885 and was the first entity to collate global statistics. The Institute was overseen by two economists at the University of Vienna who were also Mises’s professors: Franz Neumann-Spallart and Franz Juraschek. As F. A. Hayek’s grandfather, Juraschek had a filial tie to the neoliberal circle.

zh: 因为在国联没有席位，美国的经济国际主义者往往借国际商会来传达自己的立场。在1919年那场将催生国际商会的大西洋城会议上，组织者解释说，战后重建世界贸易本身就是一场斗争。美国政府的孤立主义立场已经造成一种奇特的反转：如今轮到欧洲工商界来为美国人解围了。大西洋城会议主席阿尔弗雷德·C. 伯德福（Alfred C. Bedford）对到场的五十位欧洲企业家说：“你们就好像一支前来解围的援军，帮助我们打通一处堵塞。战争摧残了世界贸易这一高度敏感的机制，由此造成的封锁威胁正迫近美国，也同样迫近欧洲。”与会的商业领袖们想象着一个本应、也亟需没有阻碍商品与资本之墙的世界。正如伯德福所说：“千百万人的物质舒适与福祉，乃至生命本身，都有赖于这套现代国际贸易机制得到恢复，有赖于铲平那些跟在战争身后筑起的壁垒，直到商路重开，使人类生存所赖的物资能够从其最丰沛之地畅流到最需之地。”
伯德福唤起了一幅世界经济的水利图景：商品流经航运与铁路基础设施开凿的“商业通道”，并以——想来如此——信息在传播网络中的自由流动为前提。这是一个没有中央控制的网络化世界经济，供求规律决定着世界资源以及人类制造的产品的分配。
en: Without a seat at the League of Nations, American economic internationalists often relied on the ICC to make their position heard. At the 1919 meeting in Atlantic City that would lead to the formation of the ICC, the organizers explained that reestablishing world trade after the war would be a struggle in itself. The isolationist position of the U.S. government had already effected a curious reversal. European business leaders now had to come to the rescue of Americans. The chair of the Atlantic City conference, Alfred C. Bedford, said to the fifty European businessmen in attendance: “It is as if you were a relief force come to assist us in raising a blockage. For against America—as much as against Europe—a blockade by the war’s havoc upon that highly sensitive mechanism of the world’s trade, threatens and impends.” The assembled business leaders imagined a world that should and needed to be free of walls obstructing goods and capital. As Bedford said, “not only the physical comfort and well-being but the very lives of millions of people, depend upon this modern mechanism of international trade being restored, upon the barriers which were erected in the wake of war being leveled, until the channels of commerce can be reopened so that the commodities upon which human existence depends, may flow unchecked from where they are most plentiful to where they are most needed.”

Bedford evoked a vision of the world economy as a hydraulic landscape. Commodities flowed through the “channels of commerce” created by the infrastructure of shipping and rails, and enabled presumably by the free flow of information in the networks of communication. This was a networked world economy without centralized control, where the laws of supply and demand dictated the distribution of the world’s resources and its man-made products.

zh: 要实现这一愿景，需要人与国家的助力。然而，借用更古老的古典自由主义想象，这一过程被描绘成自然的过程，仿佛源自物理学规律，甚至万有引力。伯德福谴责战争期间筑起的“壁垒”，指的是世界各地为保护生产和国家自给自足而采取的贸易保护措施。在与会企业家口中，这些成了背离自然状态的人为障碍。这些隐喻呼应了伍德罗·威尔逊自己在“十四点”中的措辞，其中一点呼吁“在一切同意和平并愿为维护和平而结合起来的国家之间，尽可能消除一切经济壁垒，确立平等的贸易条件”。
en: Human and state facilitation was needed to realize this vision. Yet, drawing from an older classical liberal imaginary, the process was depicted as natural, stemming from the laws of physics, perhaps even gravity. Bedford condemned the “barriers” raised during the war, referring to protectionist measures throughout the world that had been designed to safeguard production and national self-sufficiency. These were portrayed by the gathered businessmen as artificial impediments to a natural state. The metaphors reflected Woodrow Wilson’s own language in the Fourteen Points, one of which called for “the removal, as far as possible, of all economic barriers and the establishment of an equality of trade conditions among all the nations consenting to the peace and associating themselves for its maintenance.”

zh: 国际商会在成立大会上，其成员宣布：“一个国家不是独立的经济单位。事实每天都在证明，各国在经济上相互依存。”
在1921年第一届大会上，国际商会已纳入战败国奥地利的代表；1923年后又有德国加入，代表来自三十三国。
到1927年，国际商会已有2300余名会员：近半数来自工业界，约四分之一来自银行业和贸易业。
1925年之后，米塞斯出任国际商会奥地利代表。他1925年赴布鲁塞尔出席第三届大会，1926年首次前往美国。作为奥地利代表，他四处奔走，并负责筹办1933年5—6月在维也纳召开的国际商会第七届大会。
en: At its constitutive session, the members of the ICC declared that “a nation is not an independent economic unit. Every day, the facts demonstrate the interdependence of all countries in the economic domain.”
At its first congress in 1921, the ICC already included representatives from the defeated Austria and, after 1923, Germany, with delegates from thirty-three countries.
By 1927 the ICC had over 2,300 members; almost half were in the field of industry, about a quarter in banking and trade.

After 1925 Mises was the Austrian representative to the ICC. He traveled to Brussels for the third congress in 1925 and to the United States for the first time in 1926. In his capacity as the Austrian representative, he traveled extensively and was responsible for organizing and carrying out the seventh congress of the ICC in Vienna in May–June 1933.

zh: 国联也在全球尺度上捍卫自由主义，但它始终坚持政治自决的原则。一家德国报纸把国际商会称为“经济国联”，并说它有一项优势：美国是其成员（美国不是国联成员）。
相信相互依存的美国实业家和银行家便在国际商会中组织起来。例如通用电气的查尔斯·戴斯（Charles Dawes）和美国银行家欧文·D. 杨（Owen D. Young），二人参与了1924年和1929年重订偿还期限和减轻战争债务负担的计划，都是积极的会员。
威利斯·H. 布思（Willis H. Booth）把戴斯计划称为国际商会的“产品”。
前副国务卿诺曼·H. 戴维（Norman H. Davis）与戴斯、杨同台演讲；时值一趟前往布鲁塞尔参加1925年国际商会第五次会议的行程之前。戴维表达了对相互依存的务实态度：“不管我们喜欢与否，我们再也不能无视世界事务了。我们作为债权国的地位，加上日益增长的市场需求，向我们施加了一项责任与义务。”
en: The League of Nations also defended liberalism on a global scale, but it remained committed to the principle of political self-determination. A German newspaper referred to the ICC as the “Economic League of Nations,” with the advantage that the United States was a member (it was not a member of the League).

U.S. businessmen and bankers with a belief in interdependence organized in the ICC. Charles Dawes of General Electric, and the American banker Owen D. Young, for example, who were involved in plans to reschedule and relieve war debts in 1924 and 1929, were both active members.
Willis H. Booth called the Dawes Plan the “product” of the ICC.

Norman H. Davis, former under secretary of state, speaking alongside Dawes and Young before a trip to the fifth meeting of the ICC in Brussels in 1925, expressed the pragmatic attitude toward interdependence: “Whether we like it or not, we cannot any longer disregard world affairs. Our position as a creditor nation, with a growing necessity for markets, imposes a duty and an obligation upon us.”

zh: 1926年以前，国际商会主要关心一项他们自称“经济重建”的任务；1926年之后，他们转而同时反对关税和非关税贸易壁垒。
他们得到 Stubenring 一伙人的积极支持。维也纳工商会经济学家理查德·赖德尔（Richard Riedl）为国际商会撰写了规模最大的报告之一，在两份出版物中呼吁降低关税。
在当时，他的工作是测算关税指数最宏大的尝试：计算覆盖402种商品、14个国家。
1920年国联接手搜集国际经济统计的任务——他们最终把这项工作做到了前所未有的完备程度——国际商会就是参与者之一。
en: Until 1926 the ICC group was primarily concerned with a task they described as economic reconstruction; after 1926 they shifted their focus to opposing both tariff and nontariff barriers to trade.

They received active support from the Stubenring group. Richard Riedl, an economist at the Vienna Chamber of Commerce, prepared one of the most extensive reports for the ICC with two publications calling for the sinking of tariffs.
At the time his was the most extensive attempt to calculate the tariff index; his calculations covered 402 commodities and fourteen countries.

When in 1920 the League of Nations took up the task of gathering international economic statistics, which they would eventually take to an unprecedented level of comprehensiveness, the ICC was one of the members.

zh: 国联经济财政处处长阿瑟·萨尔泰（Arthur Salter）说，国际商会关于削减贸易壁垒的报告，正是1927年世界经济会议的基石。
他描述了两个机构之间的分工：国际商会拥有“对行政行为实际效果的直接体验”，国联则拥有“商会作为私人机构所不具备的、直接且正式参与各国政府磋商与各部门行动的渠道”。“如果国联能提供实现行政改革的机器，它在很大程度上必须向诸位寻求动力。”他在对国际商会会员的演说中说。首要目标是消极性的——移除壁垒。“我们携手从事的实际任务，几乎全都在于设法改变那些妨碍生意的政策或行政办法。”
en: Arthur Salter, head of the of the League of Nations Economic and Financial Section, described the ICC’s report on the reduction of trade barriers as the foundation of the World Economic Conference of 1927.

He described a division of labor between the two organizations, with the ICC having “direct experience of the practical effects of administrative action” and the League having “a direct and official entry into the coun-sels of governments and the action of departments which the Chamber, as a private institution does not possess.” “If the League can offer the machinery for achieving administrative reform, it must look to you for much of the motive force,” he said in an address to the ICC’s members. The primary goal was the negative one of removing barriers. “The actual tasks on which we are working together nearly all consist in trying to modify policies or administrative methods which impede business.”

zh: 就在这些月份里，商业国际主义者找到了他们的反壁垒事业最持久的象征。关税壁垒的故事，是隐喻如何变成经济政策的一个颇具启示的个案。故事始于1926年：英国下议院议员、曾任温斯顿·丘吉尔议会私人秘书的克莱夫·莫里森-贝尔，收听到一则关于贸易保护政策的广播报道，由此确信欧洲各国“正在慢慢走向自我毁灭”。他开始寻找描绘经济关系的视觉手段，以说明欧洲是“一个庞大的共同体，其成员同沉同浮”。
en: In these months, business internationalists found the most enduring symbol for their campaign against barriers. The story of the tariff wall is a telling case study in how metaphors turn into economic policy. It begins in 1926, after Clive Morrison-Bell, an English Member of Parliament and former parliamentary private secretary to Winston Churchill, heard a radio report on protectionist policies that convinced him that European “countries were slowly committing suicide.” He set out to find a visual means of depicting economic relationships to show that Europe was “one large community, the members of which would sink or swim together.”

zh: 莫里森-贝尔委托当地一名木匠制作了一张桌面大小的欧洲地图，每个国家周围围着微缩的红砖墙。每堵墙的高度对应该国关税的平均水平，但莫里森-贝尔惊讶地发现，政府自己都没有这份数据。他只好求助国联，国联把该年代之初就开始搜集的数字提供给了他。地图后来的一个版本上有一个黑体大字标题：“把这个观念可视化”（Visualize the Idea）。这里呈现的是什么观念？桌面版地图上那些漆成红色的墙，给人的第一印象是欧洲各国危险而时代错置的自我封闭。在莫里森-贝尔《关税壁垒》（Tariff Walls）一书的序言中，代阿伯农子爵（Viscount D'Abernon）写道，地图上的这片大陆“最像一组中世纪的设防营寨，专为阻碍进步而设”。
en: Morrison-Bell commissioned a local carpenter to build a table-size map of Europe with miniature red brick walls circling each country. The height of each wall was to correspond to the averaged level of the country’s tariffs, but Morrison-Bell found to his surprise that the government itself did not have this data. He had to turn to the League of Nations, which supplied him with the numbers that they had begun gathering at the beginning of the decade. A later version of the map had a boldface title: “Visualize the Idea.” What idea was represented here? The first impression of the walls, painted red in the table-sized version, is of the European nations’ hazardous and anachronistic self-encapsulation. In the foreword to Morrison-Bell’s book
the Viscount D’Abernon wrote that the continent on the map “resembles nothing so much as a group of medieval fortified camps designed to impede progress.”

zh: 这正是莫里森-贝尔希望他的地图所呈现的局面。他认为自己是在运用“大众心理学的基本要素——任何进步，无论多么有限，其最好的希望都取决于这些要素”，而要传播这一观念，“没有比通过眼睛、借助这种略显新奇的制图方式更简便的办法了”。
他解释了关税壁垒上砖块的视觉隐喻如何让经济变得可见——并指出这一说法很快流行开来。他问道：
en: This was precisely the situation Morrison-Bell intended his map to portray. He saw himself using the “elementary lines of mass psychology that the best hope of any progress, however moderate, depends, and for propagating this idea there can be no simpler method than through the eye by means of this somewhat novel form of cartography.”
He explained how the visual metaphor of the bricks in the tariff wall made the economic visible—and noted that it caught on quickly. Who would have spoken, he asked

zh: 几年前，有谁会说要在关税墙上多砌一层砖？人们本来不得不为这个简单的比喻作长篇解释。因此，哪怕仅做到这一步，也许也有些用处，因为其他国家的公众一旦开始……开始被这样一种想法攫住——他们之所以无法尽享生活必需品，是因为自己仿佛被一堵砖墙圈了起来——那么另一个想法也许就会开始生根，即：大家齐心协力从这些墙的顶部敲掉几块砖，也许并不是多难的事。
en: about putting a course of bricks on a tariff wall a few years ago. It would have been necessary to go into long explanations about this simple simile. So to have accomplished even this may be of some use, for the moment the public in other countries begin . . . to be seized with the idea that they are prevented from enjoying to the full the necessaries of life, because they are walled in as though with a brick wall, the further idea might begin to take root, namely, that it might not be a very difficult operation by a concerted effort to knock a few bricks off the top of these walls.

zh: 这张地图以视觉方式论证：应拆除贸易壁垒。
en: The map argued visually for the removal of the barriers to trade.

zh: 莫里森-贝尔带着这张地图周游的路线，勾勒出1920年代为“平坦世界”（flat world）鼓与呼的一处处现场。他先在英格兰银行亮相，蒙塔古·诺曼（Montagu Norman）于1926年欢迎并展出了这张地图。
随后他在伦敦证券交易所展示它，接着在巴黎国际商会总部的会议上展出，地图就在商会会长的办公室里拼装起来。之后，他在万国宫（Palace of Nations）为1927年世界经济会议召开的预备会议上展出地图，展台设在大门厅里，全体代表入场时都能看到。皇家贸易委员会主席阿瑟·巴尔福爵士（Sir Arthur Balfour）带着拆成数块的地图奔走柏林和哥本哈根，每到一地便重新组装。
哥伦比亚大学校长、卡内基国际和平基金会主席尼古拉斯·默里·巴特勒（Nicholas Murray Butler）把地图的照片分发给1500家美国报纸。
莫里森-贝尔声称，他的模型把“关税壁垒”（tariff walls）这个隐喻性说法作为“关税障碍”（tariff barriers）或“贸易障碍”（obstacles to trade）的同义词带进了公共讨论——此说并非虚言。
1926年底，《纽约时报》（
）通栏刊登了这张地图的图片，图注为“关税‘墙’”。
en: Morrison-Bell’s itinerary of travels with the map traces the sites of advocacy for the flat world in the 1920s. He began with the Bank of England, where Montagu Norman welcomed and displayed the map in 1926.

Then he showed it at the London Stock Exchange, followed by a meeting at the headquarters of the ICC in Paris, where it was constructed in the president’s room. Next he displayed it at the preparatory meeting for the 1927 World Economic Conference at the Palace of Nations, in a foyer to be seen by all delegates as they entered. The chairman of the Royal Commission on Trade, Sir Arthur Balfour, traveled to Berlin and Copenhagen with the map in pieces, assembling it on his arrival.
Nicholas Murray Butler, president of both Columbia University and the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, circulated photographs of the map to 1,500 American newspapers.
Morrison-Bell claimed plausibly that his model brought the metaphorical term “tariff walls” into public discussion as a synonym for “tariff barriers” or “obstacles to trade.”
An image of the map appeared across the full width of a page in the
in late 1926, with the legend “Tariff ‘walls.’ ”

zh: 1927年3月，莫里森-贝尔在奥地利议会的预算厅展出了他的模型，随后在 Stubenring 的工商会展出；他评论道，这家机构“不同于英国的同类机构，似乎是一个与政府关系密切的半官方团体”，这一观察切中实情。
工商会会员们大感兴趣，请他专门为商会另做一个版本；莫里森-贝尔于1929年交付，此图随后被用作巡回教具，投入“为改善中欧商业条件而进行的斗争”。
en: In March 1927 Morrison-Bell displayed his model in the budget room of the Austrian parliament, and then to the Chamber of Commerce on the Stubenring, which he remarked correctly was “unlike similar institutions in England, seems to be a semi-official body closely connected with the Government.”

The members of the Chamber were so intrigued that they requested their own version of the map, which Morrison-Bell delivered in 1929 to be used as a traveling pedagogical instrument in the “struggle for an improvement of the commercial conditions in Central Europe.”

zh: 最醒目的展示还是在1927年世界经济会议本身。莫里森-贝尔事先就打算把地图放大许多倍。按计划，地图将在日内瓦湖畔铺开二十平方码。
在这个放大版中，低关税国家的轮廓从上方看仍清晰可辨，别国则显得扭曲变形，被路障挤歪了形状。让熟悉的欧洲轮廓变得陌生，正是其用意所在。莫里森-贝尔把1927年世界经济会议期间的一幅荷兰漫画翻印为自己书的卷首插图：画中“欧洲的关税壁垒”堆成一座既令人眩晕又令人望而生畏的高墙，让前景里那个小小的人影迷失方向、望而生畏。
en: The most visible display was at the 1927 World Economic Conference itself. Morrison-Bell planned beforehand to scale up the map considerably. The map was to stretch over twenty square yards on the shores of Lake Geneva.

In this grand form the contours of countries with low tariffs would be easily recognizable from above, while others would appear warped, their shape distorted by barricades. Making the familiar profile of Europe strange was intentional. As the frontispiece to his book, Morrison-Bell reprinted a Dutch cartoon from the World Economic Conference in 1927 that depicted a towering heap of “tariff walls in Europe” that was both disorienting and daunting to the small figure in the foreground.

zh: 在大幅地图的制作上历经周折之后，莫里森-贝尔还是在日内瓦湖畔一栋专供展出的建筑里，展出了一个较小比例的模型。在那里，他收到赖德尔为维也纳工商会撰写的报告副本。报告中附有一张地图，依相对关税水平施加深浅不同的阴影色。其计算远比莫里森-贝尔此前得到的数据浩大：国联只搜集78种商品的价格数据，而 Stubenring 上的国际商会奥地利分会搜集的数据覆盖402种商品。
莫里森-贝尔把这张地图与自己的并置展出。奥地利与英国自由主义者的想象彼此渗透，为各自的自由贸易诉求创造出一套共同的视觉语言。
en: After having troubles with construction of the large-scale map, Morrison-Bell set up a smaller-scale model in Geneva in a dedicated building on the lakeshore. While there, he received a copy of a report from the Vienna Chamber of Commerce prepared by Riedl. It included a map with shading according to relative tariff levels. The calculations were much more extensive than Morrison-Bell’s previous data. The League of Nations was collecting price data on only 78 goods; the Austrian branch of the ICC on the Stubenring was collecting data on 402 goods.
Morrison-Bell displayed the map alongside his own. The imaginaries of Austrian and English liberals were interpenetrating, creating a common visual language for their demands for free trade.

zh: 1927年5月的世界经济会议与同年7月国际商会斯德哥尔摩大会，都把反对贸易壁垒作为其宣示的核心。正如威廉·拉帕德（William Rappard）后来所指出的，关键在于：“这些建议的权威，不只来自几个昏聩的自由派教授，更来自一场规模庞大的代表性集会，其中甚至包括美国实业界人士——谁也不能指责他们是空想的国际主义者。”

商界的参与，标志着他们日益愿意承担积极的公共角色。他们显然也更热衷于把学术专长纳入自身意见的形成过程。国际商会主席说：“每当世界需要了解实业界人士的看法时，它总是越来越多地求助于我们。继国联之后，各大国际机构——农业、交通与运输等等——一个接一个地请我们协助工作。我们声称负有代表商界发言的责任，如今这一主张已获各方承认。我们不能辜负寄予我们的期望。Noblesse oblige（位高责重），如果允许我这么说的话，我们自身的利益也如此要求。”
商界的国际主义在经济专业知识的襄助下，正在推动确立一条关于世界经济应当如何运转的新规范。
en: Both the World Economic Conference in May 1927 and the Stockholm Conference of the ICC in July made opposition to trade barriers central to their message. It was key, William Rappard noted later, that “these recommendations were made on the authority not only of a few benighted liberal professors, but of a large representative gathering, including even American business men, whom no one could denounce as visionary internationalists.”

The participation of the business community signaled an increasing willingness to take an active public role. They were also evidently more keen to draft academic expertise into the formulation of their opinions. The ICC president said, “The world turns more and more to us whenever it needs to ascertain the views of business men. Following the example of the League of Nations, great international institutions one after another, for agriculture, for communications and transit, appeal to us to assist them in their work. We claimed the responsibility of representing business and now that claim is admitted on all sides. We must not disappoint the hopes placed in us. Noblesse oblige, and if you will permit me to say so, our own interest demands.”
Business internationalism, with the aid of economic expertise, was helping to standardize a new norm about how the world economy should operate.

zh: 一张同时代的照片拍到克莱夫·莫里森-贝尔站在他的地图旁俯看模型，地点是维也纳工商会。说明牌上用法语写着：“鸟瞰欧洲经济”（A Bird's-Eye View of Economic Europe）。正如那些常常着迷于营造从空中看赏心悦目的对称格局的现代建筑师或城市规划师，这张关税地图也在塑造它自己的解决方案，鼓励人们去实现一个不再被墙壅塞的世界。这种立场并非地图在自由派实业家中催生出来的，但它使这种立场结晶定型，并且如莫里森-贝尔所预感的那样，把它投射为一种更具说服力的形式——无论这些墙对普通人或评论者的实际生活产生什么效果，这套图说都让论证更能动人。
en: A contemporary photograph shows Clive Morrison-Bell standing over his map at the Vienna Chamber of Commerce. The placard reads, in French, “A Bird’s-Eye View of Economic Europe.” As with the modern architects or urban planners who were often drawn to produce symmetries below pleasing to the eye in the sky, the tariff map shaped its own solutions, encouraged the realization of a world uncluttered by walls. The map did not produce this position among liberal businessmen but it crystallized and, as Morrison-Bell intuited it would, projected it in a form that made the argument more compelling to both the common person and the commentator, regardless of its actual effects on their lives.

zh: 这个隐喻自带其言外之意。米塞斯在工商会的门生戈特弗里德·哈伯勒指出，要为关税壁垒的“高度”（他特意加了引号）算出单一数字，需要多少偷梁换柱。且不论各产品关税千差万别这一现实，关税通常还是两国间条约议定的，也就是说，站在哪个国家的视角去看，地图的样子就不同。
“单一关税壁垒”的观念暗中带出了最惠国（Most-Favored-Nation）模式的观念，即：对某一国降低关税，便会自动降低对所有其他国家的关税。这一规范在1927年世界经济会议上针对美国关税被确立下来；它在保护主义盛行的1930年代土崩瓦解，直到第二次世界大战后关税与贸易总协定（General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade，GATT）创建才卷土重来。
en: The metaphor carried its own implications. Mises’s protégé at the Chamber of Commerce, Gottfried Haberler, pointed out the legerdemain required to create a single number for the “height” (his quotation marks) of tariff walls. Beyond the reality of varying tariffs from product to product, tariffs were also usually settled on in treaties between two countries, meaning that the map would look different depending on whose perspective one saw it from.

The single tariff wall idea carried the idea of the Most-Favored-Nation model implicitly, that is, the idea that the reduction of a tariff toward one country would involve lowering those for all other countries automatically. This norm was enshrined at the 1927 World Economic Conference against U.S. tariffs; it would crumble in the protectionist 1930s, only to return with the creation of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) after the Second World War.

zh: 城市中的路障，1927年7月
这张关税壁垒地图把欧洲做成内部筑墙的模型，从中表达了一种关于自由流动的、隐含的规范愿景。但值得注意的是，地图反映的是商品，不是人。哈伯勒写道：“包含‘经济战线’‘防御阵地’这类说法的军事语言，尤其不适用于分析国际贸易问题与国家间的分工问题……它暗示经济冲突的‘战线’永远横亘在两国之间，而实际上，冲突是在每个国家‘内部’利益不同的群体之间展开的。”
米塞斯愿景的一个面向，是拆除针对商品的壁垒以让价格趋同；另一个面向，则是必须消除工资趋同的障碍。在1920年代的奥地利，后者面临的最大挑战就是工会。米塞斯最早的刊印作品写于1906年，当时他还是一名年轻学生，他问道：英国和德国工人是否“也许不得不降到印度人和苦力那样低下的生活水平，才能与之竞争”？
1919年，他给出了一个两面兼顾的回答：一面，在他设想的世界经济中，欧洲工人的收入无疑会低于他们已习以为常的水平；另一面，全世界的“印度人和苦力”收入则会更高。米塞斯写道，一旦抛弃大卫·李嘉图在拓展空间分工范围问题上的那种古怪犹豫，“就会看到一种趋向遍及整个地球：各地的资本收益率和劳动工资分别趋于均等。到那时，最终将不再有较穷和较富的民族，只有人口稠密与稀疏、垦耕发达与粗疏的国家”。
en: In its maquette of an internally walled Europe, the tariff walls map expressed an implicit normative vision of free movement. Yet it is notable that the map reflects commodities, not people. Haberler wrote that “military language, containing expressions such as ‘economic front’ and ‘defensive positions,’ is especially inappropriate to the analysis of problems of international trade and of division of labor between countries. … It suggests that a ‘front’ of economic conflict lies always between two countries, whereas in reality the conflict is between groups having different interests
each country.”

If one side of Mises’s vision was removing barricades to goods to allow for price convergence, the other was the need to remove obstacles to wage convergence. The biggest challenge to this in 1920s Austria was the trade unions. In one of his first published works, Mises asked as a young student in 1906 whether “English and German workers may have to descend to the lowly standard of life of the Hindus and coolies to compete with them.”

In 1919 he provided a mixed answer: on the one hand, in the world economy he imagined the European worker would certainly earn less than he had become accustomed to. On the other hand, the “Hindus and coolies” of the world would earn more. Once one abandoned David Ricardo’s odd hesitation at expanding the scope of the spatial division of labor, Mises wrote, “then one sees a tendency prevail over the entire earth toward equalization of the rate of return on capital and of the wage of labor. Then, finally, there no longer are poorer and richer nations but only more densely and less densely settled and cultivated countries.”

zh: 首要的问题也最是明摆着的一个：欧洲工人不愿为了自由主义这一更高律令降薪，也不愿——按照米塞斯的论证——为了远处一个大概是非白人的外国工人的利益而降薪。1920年代自由主义面临的诸多挑战，都发端于这一障碍。米塞斯思虑及全球，却必须在地方上行动，而他所在的城市正以社会党人主政闻名于世。红色维也纳（Red Vienna）的现实，既是对这个即将成为新自由主义者的一群人所怀抱愿景之实现的挑战，也构成了冲突——而与这座社会主义者执政城市的冲突，恰恰激发了他们的思想。
en: The primary problem was the most obvious one: the unwillingness of European workers to accept lower wages for the sake of either the higher law of liberalism or, as in Mises’s argument, the benefit of a distant, likely nonwhite, foreign worker. Many of the challenges to liberalism in the 1920s proceeded from this obstacle. As Mises thought globally, he had to act locally, in a city famously governed by socialists. The realities of Red Vienna were a challenge to the realization of the vision of the group that would become the neoliberals—and conflict with the socialist-run city inspired their ideas.

zh: 米塞斯1920年代的政策处方历来有两面：向世界市场开放，并完成参与国际竞争所必需的国内调整。这需要两项关键措施：压低工资，减轻工业企业的税负。在1918年之后的著述中，他反复申明：像奥地利这样的小国根本没有自给自足的能力。这种幻想或许能在拥有巨大国内市场的国家维持（至少维持一阵）——比如美国，比如拥有帝国和自治领的英国，甚至德国——但《圣日耳曼条约》已使奥地利这个仅有六百多万人口的国家，在原材料上严重依赖外国市场。用一位美国记者的话说，它已被削减成“残破的躯干”。
1945年之后非殖民化（decolonization）浪潮中各国将面对的许多困境，在此已现端倪：奥地利帝国的终结，意味着对进入开放的世界经济的依赖加深。
en: Mises’s policy prescriptions in the 1920s always had two sides: open to the world market, and make the internal adjustments necessary to compete internationally. This required two key measures: push down wages, and cut taxes on industry. In his writings after 1918 he repeated the point that a small country like Austria had no capacity to be self-sufficient. Such a fantasy could be maintained (at least for a while) in countries with enormous domestic markets—like the United States, England with its empire and dominions, or even Germany—but the Treaty of Saint Germain had made Austria, a country of just over six million people, heavily reliant on the foreign market for raw materials. In the words of one American journalist, it had been reduced to a “mutilated torso.”
Prefiguring many of the dilemmas that would face nations after decolonization after 1945, the end of Austria’s empire meant an increased reliance on access to an open world economy.

zh: 1921年2月，米塞斯应一位政治人物之请撰写政策纲领，把问题表述得条理分明：“奥地利需要自由贸易。”在建议取消进口禁令和港口限制的同时，米塞斯还主张把公营企业私有化、取消食品补贴，并且——与其自由流动的信念一致——取消外国人的入境和居留限制。
1920年以后，工商会承担为政府撰写法律评估的职责。
在一篇立场声明中，米塞斯重申：“奥地利的未来取决于自由贸易”；奥地利的货物“要能在国外竞争”，工资就必须降到“远低于战前的水平”。
en: Mises put the issue systematically in a policy program written at the request of a politician in February 1921: “Austria needs free trade.” Alongside suggestions to lift prohibitions on imports and ports, Mises suggested privatizing public enterprises, eliminating food subsidies, and, consistent with his belief in free movement, lifting entry and residence restrictions for foreigners.
After 1920 the Chamber of Commerce had the duty of writing evaluations of laws for the government.

In a position statement, Mises restated the points that “Austria’s future depends on free trade” and that if their goods were “to be able to compete abroad,” wages would have to fall “far below their prewar level.”

zh: 阶级正义之争在1927年7月中旬轰然爆发于环城大道。导火索早在六个月前点燃：右翼民兵组织“前线战士联合会”（Frontkämpfer）在社会民主党势力雄厚的城区举行游行，遭到社民党民兵骚扰后，他们向人群开枪，打死一名工人和一个孩子。六个月后，备受瞩目的审判结果出炉——被告被彻底开释，工人们视之为司法标准倾斜的明证，群情激愤。尽管由温和派奥托·鲍威尔（Otto Bauer）领导的社会民主党劝告不要采取暴力回应，基层工人却不同意。次日清晨8时，电业工人停开有轨电车，使全城劳动力的流动陷于停摆，发出了总罢工的信号。
工人们向议会进发——议会坐落在环城大道的另一头，与工商会遥遥相对。司法宫成为众怒指向判决的靶心：一部分人冲进大楼纵火，另一部分人拦阻消防车、割断水带、打开其他消防龙头以降低水压，以这些对抗行动妨碍城市运转。
en: The fight over class justice exploded onto the Ringstrasse in mid-July 1927. The precipitating event had come six months earlier when members of the right-wing militia Frontkämpfer marched in a heavily Social Democratic area. Harassed by members of the Social Democratic militia, the Frontkämpfer fired into the crowd, killing a worker and a child. Six months later, the result of their closely watched trial was complete acquittal, enraging workers who saw it as a case of skewed standards. Though the Social Democratic Party, led by the moderate Otto Bauer, advised against a violent response, rank-and-file workers dissented. At 8:00 a.m. the following day, the electric workers stopped the streetcars, bringing the circulation of labor through the city to a halt and signaling the call to a general strike.

Workers marched to the Parliament on the far side of the Ringstrasse from the Chamber of Commerce. The Palace of Justice became the target of their anger at the court’s verdict, and part of the crowd stormed the building and set it on fire, while others blocked fire trucks, cut hoses, and opened up other hydrants to reduce water pressure, defiantly impeding the city’s functions.
